se8639f9b8b68fd: This feature mainly addresses performance bottlenecks in high-performance computing (HPC) and AI large model training settings. When a task requires the use of 2, 4, 8 or more GPUs, if these GPUs communicate only through relatively slow PCI bus lines, data exchange becomes shortboards that seriously affect overall training efficiency. If they can be scheduling to a NVLink fast interconnected GPS portfolio, data exchange will multiply, thereby maximizing faster calculation tasks.
s9ab0e380bd389e: It is based on a core principle:
s95019979428e13: Priority is given to the most compatible tasks while retaining, to the maximum extent possible, a large and complete architecture for future tasks.
s53d156cbd7ff55: Its core is divided into the following phases: “Registration of registration” and “Scheduling decision-making”;
s08a39bdb875284: Phase 1: Top-up registration - visible physical layout
s4c1c0407300461: The objective of this phase is to translate the invisible GPU physical connection at each node into standardized data that cluster Scheduler understands.
s84d33dbf503797: Information detection: On each GPU node, DevicePlugin will access all physical connection types between the two GPUs through NVML of NVIDIA, identifying precisely which are connected via high-speed NVLink and which are connected by regular PCIe bus lines.
s210a26a752a3f8: Data modelling: The results of the detection were constructed into a clear “connection matrix.” This is essentially a two-dimensional table that records any connection between the GPUs (“NVLink” or “PCIe”). This matrix is the digital blueprint for the nodal structure.
sb2bc618f872c7e: Public registration: The system converts this "connection matrix" into a JSON text and adds it to that node as an annex. By doing so, the physical expansion of the node is from a local information to a global data that is visible and searchable for the whole cluster.

sdb3570640e1ec8: Core pain point: the two limitations of original ResourcesQuota
s4fe8cd07a5a29c: Original ResourcesQuota calculates each resource independently and does not understand its intrinsic relevance. For example, when a Pod requests two GPUs each allocated to 2000 MB GPU memory (nvidia.com/gpu: 2, nvidia.com/gpumem: 2000), the original Quota mistakenly recorded total GPU demand as 2000MB instead of the correct 2 *2000MB = 4000MB. This leads to serious distortions in quota management.
s796f21306952f6: For requests for GPU memory in percentage terms (e.g. gpumem-percentage: 50), the actual consumption of GPU memory can only be calculated after decision-making by scheduling (i.e. which physical part of the GPU has been specifically assigned). The original RessourceQuota is examined before scheduling, and cannot handle this dynamic resource value that requires “scheduling before deduction”.
s3693740ad4f0d9: HAMi has introduced an extension mechanism for ResourceQuota that allows it to process complex resource requests related to GPU devices intelligently. The HAMi solution consists mainly of two core enhancements:
s0b6f99ed66afc0: Smart correlation calculations: HAMi Scheduler can identify multiple GPU resources in the same Pod request and link them to calculate them. For example above, HAMi correctly calculates the total GPU memory request to 2 (GPU) * 2000MB = 4000MB. This ensures that ResourcesQuota accurately reflects real resource consumption.
s0ee1cfba7faca8: Dynamic real-time calculations: HAMi will dynamically calculate and include quotas for requests based on percentages or no specified values in Scheduling's decision-making, based on the actual specifications of the physical GPU to be assigned to Pod. For example, if a 50 per cent GPU memory request is scheduling to a 24GB GPU, ResourcesQuota will accurately deduct 12GB.
